name: Vanadium sesquioxide
equilibrium_context: Antiferromagnetic Mott insulator (monoclinic) to paramagnetic metal (corundum) at 150 to 180 K; prototype of the Mott-Hubbard transition
summary: Two cleanly separable driven states: a light-stabilized monoclinic metallic phase that does not exist in equilibrium, and a THz-field-driven transition with a documented crossover from electronic to thermal dynamics.

driven_states.emergent_property: Light stabilizes the monoclinic metallic phase, which does not exist in equilibrium or in homogeneous material. It arises only when photoexcitation acts on the nanotextured, strained monoclinic low-temperature phase.
further_sources: Lantz et al., Nat. Commun. 8 (2017), doi:10.1038/ncomms13917 (A1g phonon hardening instead of softening, strong non-thermal argument)
Amano et al., Nat. Phys. (2024), doi:10.1038/s41567-024-02628-4 (propagation via photoinduced strain waves)
driven_states.caveat: Well justified as non-thermal: an A1g phonon hardening excludes pure overheating, since heating leads to softening. But Amano et al. show that in granular films the transition is carried by a photoinduced strain wave and does not occur in single crystals - so it is strongly morphology-dependent, not purely electronic. The Ronchi interpretation hinges on a Landau-Ginzburg model and has not been independently reproduced.

driven_states.emergent_property: An intense THz field pulse triggers an instantaneous sub-picosecond insulator-metal transition and thereby bypasses the thermal regime of the purely electrically driven transition, which sets in only after some tens of picoseconds via Joule heating.
driven_states.source: Giorgianni, Sakai & Lupi, Nat. Commun. 10, 1159 (2019), doi:10.1038/s41467-019-09137-6
further_sources: Nat. Commun. 11 (2020), doi:10.1038/s41467-020-16752-1 (non-thermal resistive switching in Mott nanowires)
driven_states.caveat: Valuable because the work addresses the thermal versus electronic question directly: it shows a temperature-dependent crossover from fast quantum-mechanical to slow thermal-dissipative dynamics. The purely electronic assignment holds only in the low-temperature, short-time window. Single group.

sources: Giorgianni, Sakai & Lupi, Nat. Commun. 10, 1159 (2019), doi:10.1038/s41467-019-09137-6
